Goals.Goal: **Disappearing membership entries are tolerated; unparseable existing entries are refused at fold.** In both measured windows of F295 — a `run/` file removed after `readdirSync` enumeration but before the callee existence check, and a file removed after that check but before the read — `listLooseEvents` omits the vanished entry and a real `ngrace cursor show` exits 0. The consequence is **not** a universal fold refusal: an interior hole refuses, a trailing event with a closer still present folds, and a vanished `opened` event is covered by the deliberate single-controller auto-open of RM-GOVERNED-PATH D8.2 with a legitimate synthesized `opened`. A malformed `<broken` loose file is **not** a disappearance: the read-only inventory may keep its filename fallback (`cursor show` exits 0), lint deliberately does not validate loose `run/` XML (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1569`), but the authoritative folding boundary refuses an existing-but-unparseable loose file (`xml.parse`, `root: null`) **before** any `discarded` write, auto-open, or ledger write, naming the file and the parse error and preserving every input byte. `EISDIR` remains a discriminating refusal; a simply absent file stays the tolerated F295 disappearance; a parseable event with omitted attributes keeps the legacy filename fallback and is not banned. The parallel `listRunOrphans` shares the late window only and is covered by a direct assertion plus a real consuming CLI path that keeps its `orphans=1` / `no-open-epoch … run/ empty` diagnostics.

**Interrupted folding recovers against the durable ledger, as the shipped contract requires.** [C-RUN-LEDGER](.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RUN-LEDGER/spec.xml)'s `AC-FOLD-ORDERING` states: *"a failure injected between write and delete leaves both the ledger and the loose files, and a follow-up fold is idempotent rather than duplicating the epoch."* The repair compares the loose event set to the durable ledger **before** loose-only closure/hole checks or synthesized auto-open can misclassify the residue, and distinguishes three cases: (i) a loose event whose id **and** canonical payload match an event in the last recorded epoch is already-recorded residue and is not re-added; when the whole loose set is such residue — the state after an interruption, including a **partial deletion of the verified prefix** — the retry reuses that epoch number, deletes the remaining loose files, and writes no new epoch and no synthesized `opened`; (ii) a loose event whose id matches **no** recorded event was newly allocated after the interruption and folds into the next epoch under the normal allocator; (iii) a loose event whose id matches a recorded event but whose canonical payload differs is a genuine conflict and is refused without writes, and a loose event whose id matches an event in an **older** recorded epoch is refused because the allocator never reuses a recorded id. Repeated interruptions remain idempotent; each event appears exactly once under the epoch that owns it; payload preservation is asserted independently through `expectedLedgerEventAttributes` plus children, never the writer's own transform.

**Mixed recovery is ordered validate-first/destroy-last with normative hook states.** The reachable mixed set — the interrupted epoch's matching residue **plus** a normally allocated fresh set **F** (ids above the ledger max) — validates all residue/conflict checks and all fresh-event foldability checks (allocation, density, closer) **before any destructive action**. An invalid fresh **F_bad** refuses with nothing deleted and no auto-open materialized; only then is the already-recorded residue deleted, the legitimate covering `opened` singleton **A** materialized when **F** requires it, the new epoch written, and the fresh loose files deleted. `injectFailureAfterResidueDelete` leaves exactly **F**; `injectFailureAfterAutoOpen` leaves exactly **F ∪ A**; both original hooks repeat against the same epoch. A named preflight mirrors fold's single-controller auto-open **in memory** and refuses before writing even when the prospective allocation set is empty.

**The deterministic `discarded` residue is closed; the two bounded boundaries are preserved.** The measured too-narrow-allocation reproduction (an event outside every allocation, `unterminated range`) that previously appended an engine-authored `discarded` before the ledger error now refuses **before** the `discarded` write: the invocation adds no file under `run/`, leaves `run-ledger.xml` byte-identical when it exists, and leaves a byte-identical `run/` set. The duplicate-event-id row (the F292.1 measurement) and the pre-existing-range-hole row refuse the same way; the repaired positive control still writes exactly one `discarded` and folds. A **controlled competing writer** that changes the stream between the preflight snapshot and the fold is retained as an explicit non-cooperating robustness case: it may still reach the stage-(ii-a) pre-ledger window with the same residue shape, and after that same actor reverses only its own mutation a real fold consumes the residue exactly once. The distinct post-ledger crash boundary comes from the `C-RUN-LEDGER`/RM-GOVERNED-PATH D3 write-verify-delete contract, **not** from F158: a fold interrupted after its ledger write may leave engine-authored partial evidence, and no criterion relabels that boundary as F158.

**The payment and the write guard are executable.** The bundle's payment set is declared exactly and its retirement-payer fixture is forced scope; the close includes the narrow payer assertion. An executable close-time discriminator covers both tracked and untracked changes against the named base commit, with a closed allowed-write set, and is proved by a planted forbidden write on a disposable fixture.
